problem: The last sentence says "At a load of 27.3 mA, IZ reaches zero and regulation ends." Regulation actually ends much earlier, when IZ falls to the 5 mA knee (load about 22.3 mA). A student can read this as "the Zener still regulates down to IZ = 0", which contradicts the knee rule taught in Section 1 and used everywhere else in the chapter.
fix: Replace with: "Regulation is lost once the load passes about 22.3 mA, where IZ falls to the 5 mA knee. At a load of 27.3 mA the Zener is fully off and the output sags to the divider value 12 × 1000/(220 + 1000) ≈ 9.8 V."

problem: IZ(max) is used in the inequality IZ(min) ≤ IZ ≤ IZ(max) before it is ever defined. IZ(min) is defined in Section 1 (knee current), but nothing in the text says what sets IZ(max).
fix: Add one line after the formula: IZ(max) is the largest current the part may carry continuously, set by its power rating and derating, that is IZ(max) = PZ(allowed)/VZ.
